claim: Uncontained high-energy debris is classified as a hazardous engine effect under 14 CFR 33.75.
evidence_excerpt: Section 33.75(g)(2)(i) defines hazardous engine effects to include: Non-containment of high-energy debris. The applicant must show that such effects will not occur under normal or failure conditions.
rationale: Evidence explicitly and directly defines uncontained high-energy debris as a hazardous engine effect.

claim: Thermal gradients across turbine airfoils contribute to cyclic thermal stresses during engine power transients.
evidence_excerpt: During engine acceleration and deceleration, large transient temperature gradients develop across the turbine airfoil cross-section, inducing substantial cyclic thermal stresses.
rationale: Evidence directly explains how transient temperature gradients induce cyclic thermal stresses.

claim: MIL-STD-1629A defines Category I severity as Catastrophic failure causing death or system loss.
evidence_excerpt: Category I - Catastrophic. A failure mode which could result in death or total weapon system loss.
rationale: Textual definition of Category I in MIL-STD-1629A exactly matches the claim.

claim: In MIL-STD-1629A Task 102, mode criticality number Cm is calculated using failure effect probability beta, failure mode ratio alpha, and part failure rate lambda_p.
evidence_excerpt: Mode criticality number (Cm) is calculated from Cm = beta * alpha * lambda_p * t, where beta is failure effect probability, alpha is failure mode ratio, and lambda_p is base part failure rate.
rationale: Exact formula and variable definitions are directly stated in the evidence.

claim: Single failure points are prioritized for retention on the Critical Items List under NASA safety standards.
evidence_excerpt: All single failure points (SFPs) that could result in loss of crew or vehicle shall be identified, documented, and submitted for retention on the Critical Items List (CIL).
rationale: Direct standard requirement mandating SFP documentation on the CIL.

claim: Rotor blade fracture can lead to high-energy fragment release if casing containment is inadequate.
evidence_excerpt: Blade loss events require containment verification to ensure released airfoil fragments cannot penetrate the surrounding engine casings and hazard aircraft structures.
rationale: Evidence confirms the physical linkage between blade loss and fragment casing penetration requirements.

claim: Turbine rotor blades undergo sustained centrifugal tension at elevated operating temperatures.
evidence_excerpt: Turbine rotor components operate under severe steady centrifugal mechanical loads combined with gas temperatures exceeding the alloy melting point.
rationale: Passage materially supports the principle of steady centrifugal loading at elevated gas temperatures.

claim: Borescope inspection enables periodic detection of airfoil surface cracking without engine disassembly.
evidence_excerpt: Periodic internal optical borescope inspections are specified in engine maintenance manuals to monitor hot-section airfoils for crack initiation and coating loss.
rationale: Evidence supports borescope inspection capability and purpose without overreaching on intervals.

claim: Under EASA CS-E 510, hazardous engine effects require demonstrated acceptable risk with extremely remote probability.
evidence_excerpt: CS-E 510(a) mandates that hazardous engine effects must be extremely remote, with cumulative probability of occurrence not exceeding 10^-7 per flight hour.
rationale: Evidence explicitly establishes the regulatory requirement and probability threshold for CS-E 510.

claim: Foreign object damage creates leading edge stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue crack propagation.
evidence_excerpt: Ingested hard debris impacting rotating compressor or turbine blades produces notches and localized plastic deformation, acting as severe stress concentrators for rapid fatigue propagation.
rationale: Direct physical explanation linking debris impact notch formation to fatigue crack acceleration.

claim: MIL-STD-1629A Category IV Minor severity denotes failure modes causing minor system degradation without damage.
evidence_excerpt: Category IV - Minor. A failure mode which results in minor system degradation without injury or major hardware damage.
rationale: Exact definition of Category IV in MIL-STD-1629A matches the claim.

claim: Fluorescent penetrant inspection is utilized to detect surface-breaking fatigue cracks during depot overhaul.
evidence_excerpt: Surface non-destructive inspection methods such as fluorescent penetrant testing (FPI) are established overhaul depot techniques for detecting micro-cracks in superalloy parts.
rationale: Directly supports use of fluorescent penetrant testing for detecting surface cracks during overhaul.

claim: Toxic products in cabin air originating from engine fluids constitute a hazardous engine effect.
evidence_excerpt: In 14 CFR 33.75(g)(2)(iv), toxic air in crew or passenger compartments in sufficient concentrations to incapacitate occupants is designated a Hazardous Engine Effect.
rationale: Exact match to regulatory definition of toxic cabin air as hazardous effect.

claim: High temperature oxidation and sulfidation degrade the protective aluminide coating on turbine airfoils.
evidence_excerpt: Exposure of turbine airfoils to sulfur-bearing combustion gases and elevated operating temperatures results in hot corrosion and accelerated oxidation of protective aluminide coatings.
rationale: Materially explains mechanism of hot corrosion/oxidation degradation on turbine coatings.

claim: In civil airworthiness safety analysis, catastrophic failure conditions must be extremely improbable.
evidence_excerpt: AC 25.1309-1B specifies that failure conditions categorized as Catastrophic must be extremely improbable, typically demonstrated by an occurrence rate less than 10^-9 per flight hour.
rationale: Direct regulatory standard mapping catastrophic condition to extremely improbable / 10^-9.

claim: Sustained high temperature exposure induces creep elongation in high pressure turbine blades.
evidence_excerpt: Creep strain accumulates over long durations under steady tensile stress and high metal temperatures, leading to permanent axial and radial elongation.
rationale: Directly supports the physical principle of creep elongation under steady stress and temperature.

claim: Loss of engine thrust control or uncommanded shutdown represents a significant propulsion hazard.
evidence_excerpt: Complete inability to modulate thrust or uncommanded engine shutdown during critical flight phases poses a major hazard to aircraft operations.
rationale: Passage confirms the operational hazard of engine thrust control loss and uncommanded shutdown.

claim: MIL-STD-1629A requires documenting failure detection methods and existing compensating provisions for each failure mode.
evidence_excerpt: Block 11 and Block 12 of the FMECA worksheet require the analyst to record method of detection and compensating provisions that reduce failure severity.
rationale: Worksheet instructions in MIL-STD-1629A explicitly require detection methods and compensating provisions.

claim: Compressor bleed air is routed through internal cooling passages to regulate hot-section component temperatures.
evidence_excerpt: Secondary cooling airflow bled from high-pressure compressor stages is directed into turbine rotor and stator cooling channels to maintain metal temperatures within design limits.
rationale: Accurately supports the thermal management function of compressor bleed air cooling.

claim: Critical Items Lists require documented engineering rationale for retention when failure modes lack redundancy.
evidence_excerpt: Items placed on the Critical Items List without redundancy must include formal retention rationale addressing design margins, testing, and inspection controls.
rationale: Direct standard instruction regarding formal retention rationale requirements for non-redundant CIL items.

claim: Thermomechanical fatigue causes turbine blade cracking.
evidence_excerpt: Foreign object damage (FOD) occurs when birds, ice, or runway gravel are ingested into the compressor inlet, causing leading edge tear and severe impact denting.
rationale: Thematic mismatch: Evidence discusses foreign object damage ingestion, providing zero evidence for thermomechanical fatigue.

claim: A borescope inspection every 500 flight cycles is mandatory.
evidence_excerpt: General FAA guidance discussing how inspection techniques and maintenance manuals help ensure continued airworthiness without specifying intervals.
rationale: Quantitative/modal overreach: General guidance on inspection does not prove or mandate an exact interval of 500 flight cycles.

claim: Hydraulic actuator spool stiction causes turbine blade uncontained disk burst.
evidence_excerpt: Hydraulic flight control actuators can experience valve spool stiction if hydraulic fluid is contaminated with particulate matter.
rationale: Severe physical and thematic mismatch: Flight control actuator spool stiction does not cause turbine disk burst.

claim: High pressure turbine blades have a certified catastrophic failure probability of zero.
evidence_excerpt: FAA AC 25.1309-1B specifies that catastrophic failure conditions must be extremely improbable, with probability on the order of 10^-9 per hour, acknowledging failure probability cannot be zero.
rationale: Contradictory claim: Regulations require extremely remote/improbable (<10^-9), explicitly rejecting claims of absolute zero probability.

claim: Fluorescent penetrant inspection can detect internal subsurface creep voids inside single crystal superalloy blades.
evidence_excerpt: Fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI) is an optical surface inspection method capable of revealing defects open to the outer surface of non-porous materials.
rationale: Contradictory physical capability: Evidence states FPI detects only defects open to the outer surface, which contradicts detecting internal subsurface creep voids.

claim: MIL-STD-1629A recommends automotive RPN thresholds above 100 to require mandatory redesign.
evidence_excerpt: MIL-STD-1629A provides quantitative mode criticality numbers and qualitative severity rankings. The standard does not use Risk Priority Numbers (RPN) or numerical RPN thresholds.
rationale: False methodology attribution: MIL-STD-1629A does not contain automotive RPN or an RPN > 100 threshold.

claim: Cooling passage blockage causes instant uncontained blade liberation within 3 seconds of throttle advance.
evidence_excerpt: Secondary cooling airflow preserves thermal equilibrium in the turbine section. Prolonged reduction in airflow results in gradual temperature elevation and accelerated creep damage.
rationale: Unsupported extreme causal timeline: Evidence notes gradual thermal elevation, contradicting instant liberation within 3 seconds.

claim: Turbine blade thermal barrier coatings completely eliminate all thermal stresses in the underlying superalloy.
evidence_excerpt: Ceramic thermal barrier coatings reduce underlying substrate metal temperature by 50 to 100 degrees C, reducing but not eliminating thermal gradients.
rationale: False absolute claim: Evidence states coatings reduce substrate temperature, directly refuting the claim that thermal stresses are completely eliminated.

claim: Engine casing containment is designed to contain catastrophic multi-stage rotor burst debris.
evidence_excerpt: AC 33.75-1A states that containment testing validates containment of a single released blade; containment of a full burst disk or multi-stage rotor burst is considered impractical.
rationale: Contradictory claim: Regulatory standard explicitly states disk burst containment is impractical, contradicting the claim that casings contain multi-stage rotor bursts.

claim: Bird ingestion into the low-pressure fan generates immediate sulfidation corrosion on turbine airfoils.
evidence_excerpt: Sulfidation occurs due to sulfur content in jet fuel reacting with hot sodium chloride deposits at metal temperatures above 700 degrees C.
rationale: Thematic and causal absurdity: Bird ingestion at the fan does not cause immediate hot-gas sulfidation corrosion in the turbine.

claim: Microstructural grain boundary sliding accelerates high temperature turbine blade deformation.
evidence_excerpt: General discussion of turbine blade alloy selection and mechanical properties under engine operating conditions.
rationale: Evidence is too high-level and generic to substantiate the specific grain boundary sliding microstructural mechanism.

claim: Modern engine designs incorporate sufficient structural margin to preclude creep rupture under typical mission profiles.
evidence_excerpt: Compliance with CS-E 510 requires evaluating structural margins across all certified engine operating regimes.
rationale: Vague regulatory statement of intent does not prove whether actual physical margins preclude creep rupture.

claim: Borescope inspection of hot section parts detects 95 percent of all fatigue cracks before rupture.
evidence_excerpt: Borescope inspections provide optical access to assess airfoil health and detect visible surface cracking.
rationale: Evidence supports optical inspection capability in general, but provides zero statistical data to verify the exact '95 percent' probability of detection.

claim: Engine vibration monitoring always warns flight crews prior to turbine blade liberation.
evidence_excerpt: Engine health monitoring and vibration sensors can detect rotor imbalance caused by severe damage or partial blade loss.
rationale: Passage states vibration sensors can detect rotor imbalance, but does not substantiate the absolute claim that it 'always warns flight crews prior to liberation'.

claim: All single point failures can be eliminated through redundant aerodynamic architectures.
evidence_excerpt: NASA-STD-8729.1A outlines methods for identifying single failure points and assessing where redundancy or operational workarounds are required.
rationale: Standard discusses identifying SFPs, but does not substantiate that all single failure points can be eliminated aerodynamically.

claim: CFM56 HPT Stage 1 blade P/N 301-789-204-0 experiences creep rupture after 5,000 cycles.
evidence_excerpt: High pressure turbine blades in gas turbine engines are subjected to high centrifugal stresses and gas temperatures that can cause creep deformation and rupture.
rationale: Component overreach: General discussion of turbine blade creep in a regulatory standard does not support an assertion about a specific CFM56 part number or cycle limit.

claim: GE90 Stage 2 High Pressure Turbine Airfoil P/N 1845M12P01 is certified for 15,000 flight hours without replacement.
evidence_excerpt: Turbine rotor life limits and maintenance intervals must be specified in the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness (ICA) submitted for engine type certification.
rationale: Component overreach: Generic requirement to submit an ICA does not support a specific 15,000 flight hour certification for GE90 P/N 1845M12P01.

claim: The CFM56-7B engine high pressure turbine blade has an operational failure rate lambda_p of 1.2e-6 failures per hour.
evidence_excerpt: MIL-STD-1629A outlines the quantitative criticality procedure using part failure rates lambda_p obtained from operational history or reliability handbooks.
rationale: Component overreach: General methodology standard does not contain proprietary CFM56-7B operational failure rates.

claim: Trent 1000 intermediate pressure compressor rotor blade P/N 451-098-112 exhibits fretting fatigue at the dovetail root.
evidence_excerpt: EASA CS-E discusses engine rotor structural integrity requirements and fatigue evaluation methodology under CS-E 510.
rationale: Component overreach: Regulatory framework does not provide specific evidence for Trent 1000 P/N 451-098-112 dovetail fretting.

claim: CFM56 HPT Stage 1 blade P/N 301-789-204-0 is susceptible to high temperature thermal fatigue.
evidence_excerpt: High temperature turbine blades in commercial turbofan engines experience cyclic thermal stresses during engine start, takeoff, and shutdown cycles that can cause thermal fatigue cracking.
rationale: Downgraded support: General turbofan turbine blade thermal fatigue principle materially supports the physical vulnerability, but cannot be DIRECT_SOURCE because the specific part number is not in the text.
